q: The concept of ____ is very important for the physical and biological sciences.
e: The concept of temperature is very important for the physical and biological sciences. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: This is because the ____ of an object is directly related to the energies of molecules composing the object.
e: This is because the temperature of an object is directly related to the energies of molecules composing the object. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Natural processes often involve energy changes and the ____ is an indicator for these changes.
e: Natural processes often involve energy changes and the temperature is an indicator for these changes. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: It is expected that students will identify that thermal energy is an ____ of a matter.
e: It is expected that students will identify that thermal energy is an internal energy of a matter. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work.

q: The sensations of hotness, warmness and coldness can be experienced by ____ objects.
e: The sensations of hotness, warmness and coldness can be experienced by touching objects. The physics in this sentence is built around touching.

q: ____ is the quantity that determines how cold (or) how hot the object is.
e: Temperature is the quantity that determines how cold (or) how hot the object is. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called ____.
e: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called thermometers. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as ____.
e: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as heat. Heat here means energy that flows because of a temperature difference. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: ____ is the energy in transit.
e: Heat is the energy in transit. Heat here means energy that flows because of a temperature difference. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: The unit of heat is the same as units of ____.
e: The unit of heat is the same as units of energy. Energy here means the capacity to do work. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, ____ flows from the first to the second body.
e: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, heat flows from the first to the second body. Heat here means energy that flows because of a temperature difference. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The motions and positions of molecules in matter result in the ____ energy and potential energy.
e: The motions and positions of molecules in matter result in the kinetic energy and potential energy. Kinetic here means energy a body has because it is moving. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the ____ of that matter.
e: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the internal energy of that matter. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: Temperature is a measure of the ____ of molecules.
e: Temperature is a measure of the internal energy of molecules. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Every thermometer uses a physical property that varies with ____.
e: Every thermometer uses a physical property that varies with temperature. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: This property is referred to as the ____ property of the thermometer.
e: This property is referred to as the thermometric property of the thermometer. Thermometric names this property.

q: For example, the thermometric property of a liquid-in-glass thermometer is the ____ of the liquid.
e: For example, the thermometric property of a liquid-in-glass thermometer is the thermal expansion of the liquid. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: The liquid-in-glass thermometer consists of a thin glass bulb joined to a ____ tube with a narrow bore which is sealed at its other end.
e: The liquid-in-glass thermometer consists of a thin glass bulb joined to a capillary tube with a narrow bore which is sealed at its other end. The physics in this sentence is built around capillary.

q: When the bulb becomes warmer, the liquid in it expands more than the bulb so some of the liquid in the bulb is forced into the ____.
e: When the bulb becomes warmer, the liquid in it expands more than the bulb so some of the liquid in the bulb is forced into the capillary tube. The physics in this sentence is built around capillary tube.

q: The thinner the bulb wall is, the ____ the response of the thermometer will be when the temperature changes.
e: The thinner the bulb wall is, the faster the response of the thermometer will be when the temperature changes. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The liquid used usually contains ____ (or) coloured alcohol.
e: The liquid used usually contains mercury (or) coloured alcohol. The physics in this sentence is built around mercury.

q: Alcohol has a lower ____ than mercury so it is more suitable for low-temperature measurements.
e: Alcohol has a lower freezing points than mercury so it is more suitable for low-temperature measurements. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Thermocouple thermometers are electrical thermometers which make use of the ____ that develops when two different metals are in contact.
e: Thermocouple thermometers are electrical thermometers which make use of the voltage that develops when two different metals are in contact. The physics in this sentence is built around voltage.

q: One of the junctions is maintained at ____ and the other junction is used as the temperature probe.
e: One of the junctions is maintained at 0℃ and the other junction is used as the temperature probe. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Because of the small size of a thermocouple junction, thermocouple thermometers are used to measure ____ changing temperatures.
e: Because of the small size of a thermocouple junction, thermocouple thermometers are used to measure rapidly changing temperatures. The physics in this sentence is built around rapidly.

q: In addition, they can be used to measure much ____ temperatures than liquid-in-glass thermometers.
e: In addition, they can be used to measure much higher temperatures than liquid-in-glass thermometers. The physics in this sentence is built around higher.

q: Resistance thermometer uses the fact that the electrical resistance of a metal (e.g platinum) wire ____ with temperature.
e: Resistance thermometer uses the fact that the electrical resistance of a metal (e.g platinum) wire increases with temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: A resistance thermometer can measure temperatures accurately in the range ____ to 1200℃ and best for steady temperatures, but it is bulky.
e: A resistance thermometer can measure temperatures accurately in the range -200℃ to 1200℃ and best for steady temperatures, but it is bulky. The physics in this sentence is built around -200℃.

q: Thermometric substances can be ____, liquids (or) gases.
e: Thermometric substances can be solids, liquids (or) gases. The physics in this sentence is built around solids.

q: They have physical properties that vary continuously and ____ with temperature.
e: They have physical properties that vary continuously and linearly with temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Temperature units depend on the ____ used.
e: Temperature units depend on the scale used. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The temperature scales most widely used today are Celsius (Centigrade), ____ and Kelvin scales.
e: The temperature scales most widely used today are Celsius (Centigrade), Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The SI unit of temperature is ____.
e: The SI unit of temperature is kelvin (K). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: To calibrate a thermometer, two ____ points are chosen and the interval between these points is subdivided into a number of equal parts.
e: To calibrate a thermometer, two reference points are chosen and the interval between these points is subdivided into a number of equal parts. The physics in this sentence is built around reference.

q: The freezing point and boiling point of water under normal ____ pressure are chosen as reference points which are marked on the thermometer.
e: The freezing point and boiling point of water under normal atmospheric pressure are chosen as reference points which are marked on the thermometer. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: The interval between these two points is divided into ____ equal parts for the Celsius scale.
e: The interval between these two points is divided into one hundred equal parts for the Celsius scale. The physics in this sentence is built around one hundred.

q: If the freezing point of water (or) ice point is marked 0℃ and the boiling point of water (or) steam point is marked ____, the thermometer scale is the Celsius scale.
e: If the freezing point of water (or) ice point is marked 0℃ and the boiling point of water (or) steam point is marked 100℃, the thermometer scale is the Celsius scale. The physics in this sentence is built around 100℃.

q: On the Celsius scale, the ice point is ____ and the steam point is 100℃.
e: On the Celsius scale, the ice point is 0℃ and the steam point is 100℃. The physics in this sentence is built around 0℃.

q: On the Fahrenheit scale the ice point is ____ and the steam point 212 F.
e: On the Fahrenheit scale the ice point is 32 F and the steam point 212 F. The physics in this sentence is built around 32 F.

q: On the Kelvin scale the ice point is ____ and the steam point is 373 K.
e: On the Kelvin scale the ice point is 273 K and the steam point is 373 K. The physics in this sentence is built around 273 K.

q: For example, normal body temperature is ____ °F.
e: For example, normal body temperature is 98.6 °F. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The relationship between the Celsius temperature $T_c$ and kelvin temperature $T_K$ is given by ____.
e: The relationship between the Celsius temperature $T_c$ and kelvin temperature $T_K$ is given by $T_c + 273 = T_K$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The lowest air temperature recorded in the world is ____.
e: The lowest air temperature recorded in the world is 184 K. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: This temperature was measured in ____ in 1983.
e: This temperature was measured in Antarctica in 1983. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: When a substance is heated, its ____ usually increases.
e: When a substance is heated, its volume usually increases. The physics in this sentence is built around volume.

q: The ____ of the substance increase correspondingly.
e: The dimensions of the substance increase correspondingly. The physics in this sentence is built around dimensions.

q: This increase in size can be explained in terms of the increased ____ energy of the molecules.
e: This increase in size can be explained in terms of the increased kinetic energy of the molecules. Kinetic here means energy a body has because it is moving.

q: The additional kinetic energy results in each molecule colliding more ____ with its neighbours.
e: The additional kinetic energy results in each molecule colliding more forcefully with its neighbours. Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed.

q: Therefore, the molecules push each other further apart and the substance which is heated increases in ____.
e: Therefore, the molecules push each other further apart and the substance which is heated increases in size. The physics in this sentence is built around size.

q: Increasing the temperature of a gas at constant ____ cause the volume of the gas to increase.
e: Increasing the temperature of a gas at constant pressure cause the volume of the gas to increase. Pressure here means force acting normally on unit area. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: This increase occurs not only for gases, but also for liquids and ____.
e: This increase occurs not only for gases, but also for liquids and solids. The physics in this sentence is built around solids.

q: In general, if the temperature of a substance increases, so does its ____.
e: In general, if the temperature of a substance increases, so does its volume. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: This phenomenon is known as ____.
e: This phenomenon is known as thermal expansion. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: You may have noticed that the concrete roadway segments of a sidewalk are separated by ____.
e: You may have noticed that the concrete roadway segments of a sidewalk are separated by gaps. The physics in this sentence is built around gaps.

q: This is necessary because concrete expands with increasing ____.
e: This is necessary because concrete expands with increasing temperature. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Without these gaps, thermal expansion would cause the segments to push against each other, and they would eventually ____ and break apart.
e: Without these gaps, thermal expansion would cause the segments to push against each other, and they would eventually buckle and break apart. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: Although two different metal bars of the same length are heated such that the increase in temperature is the same, the ____ of their expansion may not be the same.
e: Although two different metal bars of the same length are heated such that the increase in temperature is the same, the magnitudes of their expansion may not be the same. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: For example, the expansion of copper is ____ times that of steel.
e: For example, the expansion of copper is one and a half times that of steel. The physics in this sentence is built around one and a half.

q: ____ expands twice as much as steel does.
e: Aluminium expands twice as much as steel does. The physics in this sentence is built around Aluminium.

q: The dependence of the change in length of an object on its original length and change in temperature is ____.
e: The dependence of the change in length of an object on its original length and change in temperature is $\Delta l = \alpha l \Delta T$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: In the formula $\Delta l = \alpha l \Delta T$, $\alpha$ represents the ____.
e: In the formula $\Delta l = \alpha l \Delta T$, $\alpha$ represents the coefficient of linear expansion. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: The coefficient of linear expansion is the change in length per ____ length for one degree change in temperature.
e: The coefficient of linear expansion is the change in length per unit length for one degree change in temperature. Unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: The unit of $\alpha$ is per K, which can be written as ____.
e: The unit of $\alpha$ is per K, which can be written as $K^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $K^{-1}$.

q: The coefficient of linear expansion for steel is ____.
e: The coefficient of linear expansion for steel is $1.27 \times 10^{-5} K^{-1}$. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: Therefore, the length of the metal bar at $T + \Delta T$ is ____.
e: Therefore, the length of the metal bar at $T + \Delta T$ is $l' = l(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$. The physics in this sentence is built around $l' = l(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$.

q: The relations analogous to the one which gives the increase in length $\Delta l$ for the increase in temperature $\Delta T$ can be derived for the area expansion and ____.
e: The relations analogous to the one which gives the increase in length $\Delta l$ for the increase in temperature $\Delta T$ can be derived for the area expansion and volume expansion. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The relation obtained for area expansion is ____.
e: The relation obtained for area expansion is $\Delta A = \beta A \Delta T$. The physics in this sentence is built around $\Delta A = \beta A \Delta T$.

q: The relation obtained for volume expansion is ____.
e: The relation obtained for volume expansion is $\Delta V = \gamma V \Delta T$. The physics in this sentence is built around $\Delta V = \gamma V \Delta T$.

q: In the equation $\Delta A =  eta A \Delta T$, $ eta$ is the ____.
e: In the equation $\Delta A = \beta A \Delta T$, $\beta$ is the coefficient of area expansion. The physics in this sentence is built around coefficient of area expansion.

q: The coefficient of area expansion of a substance is the change in area per unit area for one ____ change in temperature.
e: The coefficient of area expansion of a substance is the change in area per unit area for one degree change in temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The coefficient of volume expansion of a substance is the change in volume per unit volume for one degree change in ____.
e: The coefficient of volume expansion of a substance is the change in volume per unit volume for one degree change in temperature. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Generally all substances expand on heating and ____ on cooling.
e: Generally all substances expand on heating and contract on cooling. The physics in this sentence is built around contract.

q: But in the case of water the behavior is different, when water at 0℃ is heated its volume decreases up to ____ and density increases.
e: But in the case of water the behavior is different, when water at 0℃ is heated its volume decreases up to 4℃ and density increases. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: At 4℃ the ____ becomes maximum and beyond this temperature volume start to increase.
e: At 4℃ the density becomes maximum and beyond this temperature volume start to increase. Density here means mass per unit volume. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: This unusual expansion of water is called ____ of water.
e: This unusual expansion of water is called anomalous expansion of water. Anomalous expansion names this unusual expansion of water.
